clue.text: Vocaliser is working in Bury

indicators.note: one thing being inside another is the plainest way to say one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A singer is busy performing in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the town in Greater Manchester, capitalised for the surface, but it is the verb meaning to put in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who intones chants or speaks in a sing-song voice, so an intoner uses their voice musically.

clue.text: Nemesis starts to vilify evil-doer in fury

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: fury is extreme anger

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Retribution begins with blackening a villain's name in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemesis is the Greek goddess of retribution; the capital letter hides that it is used as a common noun for one who punishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an agent of deserved retribution, someone who exacts punishment for a wrong, which is exactly an avenger.

clue.text: Rose's inelegant disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement or placing, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose has a clumsy, awkward temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose reads as a woman's name with a possessive, and disposition as her temperament; the 's is really 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is another name for the sweetbriar, a wild species of the flower with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Victim I defended is revealed to be fearful

indicators.note: something revealed is uncovered from where it lay concealed in the clue's own letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A lawyer's client turns out, after the defence, to be a frightened person.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a run of consecutive letters straddling three words of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone lacking courage and easily frightened; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Policeman holding Henry's egg-beater

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grasp, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: copper is informal for a police officer
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A police officer has seized Henry's kitchen whisk.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg-beater suggests a kitchen whisk, but it is slang for a helicopter, from the whirling blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-beater and chopper are both slang names for a helicopter, after the beating motion of its rotor.

clue.text: Even a place of higher eduction has class

parts.note: uni is short for university
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Even a university has social standing, the clue claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eduction' is a misprint for education in the printed clue. In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means consistent and unvarying throughout, the same sense as even or regular.

clue.text: Cashiers fish from the side of the ditch

parts.note: those who count money, as cashiers do
the carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Bank tellers go fishing from the edge of a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish looks like a verb, as if the cashiers are angling, but it is a noun giving a species.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification the counterscarp is the outer wall or slope of a defensive ditch, facing the scarp.

clue.text: "This is for breakfast? Love a duck!", Mark interjected

indicators.note: to interject is to throw something in between, so a piece is inserted into the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written
the teal is a small duck
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone served an odd breakfast exclaims 'Love a duck!', and Mark chips in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love a duck!' is an old British exclamation of surprise, but here it splits into three pieces. The definition is a cryptic question: what is this that is eaten at breakfast?
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal, ground oats cooked as porridge, is a traditional breakfast food, so the question points to it.

clue.text: His room is refurbished in a style seen in Spain

definitions.text: in a style seen in Spain

indicators.note: a refurbished place has been done up and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's bedroom is redecorated in a Spanish style.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'in a style seen in Spain' describes a style, matching an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorish architecture, with horseshoe arches and tiles, survives across southern Spain, notably the Alhambra in Granada.

clue.text: Analyst leads woman round bowling area

parts.note: to lead is to head, as in heading a team

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman
a rink is the strip of green used in a game of bowls

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst guides a woman around the bowling green.
explanation.walkthrough: A rink in lawn bowls is a section of the green where one match is played, not only an ice rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Headshrinker is jocular slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst, someone who treats the mind.

clue.text: In the middle of the day horse is in shape

indicators.note: being in something places it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: noon is midday
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: At midday the horse is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In shape' reads as an idiom for fitness, but 'in' belongs to the container signal and shape alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a specific plane figure with nine sides, an example of a geometric shape.

clue.text: Embassy official loses car certificate

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so part is dropped from the word

parts.note: a diplomat works at an embassy
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A consular officer has his car taken away and gets a document.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for car via the Ford Model T, a common crossword shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document awarded on completing a course of study, a kind of official certificate.

clue.text: Mistake has tinker guillotined

indicators.note: a guillotine cuts off the head, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a tinker is a mischievous child, as is a little terror

explanation.surface: A blunder means an itinerant mender has been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinker suggests the travelling pot-mender, but in Britain it is also a mischievous child, a little terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake and an error are plain synonyms for something done wrongly or inaccurately.

clue.text: Dunce is amusing or unruly

indicators.note: unruly things will not stay in order, so the letters fall out of their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The class dunce is either funny or badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amusing or unruly' reads as a description of the dunce, but 'or' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name an ignorant or stupid person; an ignoramus is someone lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Bond to observe hesitation when taking hold of breast

indicators.note: taking hold of something means gripping it inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to note is to observe
pap is an old word for a nipple or breast
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A tie between people means noticing reluctance when clutching at the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like a tie or a financial bond, but bond is a high-quality writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond paper is a strong, good-quality writing stock often used for letters, so it is a type of notepaper.

clue.text: Suspend hospital department? That's severe!

parts.note: to string something up is to hang it
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Someone proposes closing a hospital department, and another protests at the harshness.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspend looks like closing down, but it means hanging, as one strings something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and demanding, exactly what severe measures or standards are.

clue.text: King holds saint to be a lawbreaker

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside your grip, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a king is a ruler
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A monarch detains a holy man on the grounds that he is a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is general: the answer is one particular kind of criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, so he is one specific kind of criminal who breaks the law.

clue.text: Feed US rhino wrongly

indicators.note: something done wrongly is not in the proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A zookeeper gives an American rhinoceros the wrong food.
explanation.walkthrough: US looks like America, but its two letters simply join the rhino's in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to provide food or sustenance needed for growth and health, a synonym for feed.

clue.text: Live wire caught round pole? It can't be helped!

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the person or thing rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something caught round another is wrapped about it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A live electric cable has got wrapped round a post, and nothing can be done.
explanation.walkthrough: Live wire suggests electricity but is an idiom for an energetic person. The exclamation is a resigned shrug at something beyond saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something past saving or doomed, so beyond any help at all.

clue.text: Footwear and books getting covered with soup

indicators.note: in a down entry, a covering lies on top, so the second piece written goes first

parts.note: gumbo is a thick soup from Louisiana
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Shoes and books end up splattered with soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece covered by another sits beneath it, so the soup comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboot is a rubber wellington boot, so it is an item of footwear.

clue.text: Greek character to vindicate form of energy

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjective, as in nuclear power

parts.note: nu is the Greek letter N
to vindicate someone is to clear their name

explanation.surface: A Greek person sets out to justify some kind of power source.
explanation.walkthrough: Character here means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power, released by splitting atoms, is a recognised kind of energy, so the word names it.

clue.text: They say a sailor's offensive

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a salt, or old salt, is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: People reckon a seaman is rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Offensive reads as an adjective, rude, but it is the noun for a military attack; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack or campaign, and an assault is an attack, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Chiton cut short initially in North Africa

definitions.note: describes where the place is rather than naming it

indicators.note: something cut has had a piece removed, here the end of the word

parts.note: a chiton is a tunic worn in ancient Greece

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A Greek garment was shortened when first worn in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' reads as one phrase, but cut alone trims the garment and 'short initially' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia, which lies on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: Write about mineral in food

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to pen is to write
mica is a silicate mineral

explanation.surface: A writer describes the minerals found in what we eat.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a less common spelling of pemmican, with one M.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is dried pounded meat mixed with fat, a concentrated provision eaten by travellers and explorers.

clue.text: A seat has nap trimmed by Leo

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: nap and pile are the raised surface of a fabric
Leo is the lion of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A chair's velvet surface is trimmed by someone called Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap suggests a short sleep, but it is the soft surface of cloth; 'by' places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the passenger seat behind the rider on a motorcycle, or historically on a horse.

clue.text: Charge makes Peter go wild

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being accused of a crime sends Peter into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like an accusation or a fee, but it is a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a person entrusted to another's care, as a protégé is guided by a patron or mentor.

clue.text: Speaker reserves royal box for arranger

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep something held back, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
a chest is a large box
R stands for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker books the royal box for a musical arranger.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker suggests the chair of the House of Commons, but it is any public speaker. The two inserted pieces go in box first, then royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestrator scores music for the instruments of an orchestra, which is the work of a musical arranger.
